transcript:
Meeting Header
Date: 2026-03-12
Time: 08:00 PT / 11:00 ET
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Solaris - Head of AI), Marcus Doyle (Solaris - Eng Manager), Leah Chen (Solaris - CTO)

Summary:
Quarterly business review focused on usage trends, cost optimization, reliability incidents, and upcoming roadmap needs for Solaris's patient triage assistant. Customer considering Dedicated capacity for predictable latency and data isolation; also requested SOC2 artifacts and benchmark runs for long-context conversation workloads.

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone thanks for joining, happy to do a quick QBR and health check. we pulled some metrics, we'll share slides but we'll keep it conversational. Aisha you good to kick off with goals for this qtr?
[00:18] Aisha Khan: Yeah thanks Jordan, um main things for us are reducing per-conversation latency, bring down cost by at least 20% relative to what we're seeing now, and make sure we can hit our compliance checklist for the pilot with St. Mary's hospital, so VPC + KMS stuff and audit logs are critical.
[00:35] Marcus Doyle: And we want to avoid the sporadic tail-latency spikes we've been seeing after 10k tokens in the session, it's impacting UX.
[00:44] Priya Kapoor: Totally, we captured those in the incident reports. quick note before we dive in, the deck link is in the chat: https://redwood.app/decks/solaris-qbr-march2026

Usage & Cost
[01:05] Jordan Lee: Quick snapshot — your weekly active sessions have grown 35% month over month since January, total token volume up 48% q/q. That growth is great but it's the reason your bill was higher than forecast.
[01:23] Leah Chen: Right, Marcus' team ramped up integrations, so more long multi-turn sessions. can you break down where cost is coming from?
[01:31] Priya Kapoor: Sure — approx breakdown: 60% from long-context generation (avg session ~8k tokens), 25% embeddings for semantic search, 15% misc (rerank, logs). We also saw suboptimal batching for a subset of traffic — small single-request bursts driving per-token overhead.
[01:49] Jordan Lee: On cost levers: batching and KV prefix caching would cut token usage on repeat prefix prompts. we prototyped a quantization recommendation (int8) that should reduce GPU cost per token on Dedicated or Private deployments.
[02:05] Aisha Khan: For compliance reasons we prefer Dedicated with customer-managed KMS, is that still the recommended path?
[02:12] Priya Kapoor: For St. Mary's pilot — yes Dedicated in a customer VPC + HSM/KMS integration is the cleanest from an audit perspective. Hosted can do encryption at rest but doesn't give you key ownership.

Reliability & Incidents
[02:30] Jordan Lee: There were two incidents last quarter — a 22-minute latency spike on Feb. 14 and a failover window during a region maintenance on Jan. 8. both were escalated and you have the postmortems in the incident folder.
[02:45] Marcus Doyle: The Feb 14 spike coincided with a burst of 30 simultaneous long-history conversations, that's what we saw on our side too.
[02:52] Priya Kapoor: Correct — the root cause was a combination of less-than-ideal batching + a kernel selection stall on the model variant. we've deployed a runtime patch that improves kernel selection heuristics and we've added a safety fallback to a compatible smaller variant for tail events.
[03:11] Leah Chen: What's our SLO compliance look like now? we need 99.9% p99 latency under 600ms for the pilot.
[03:20] Priya Kapoor: Current p99 is 580ms for standard 2k token requests, for the 8-10k token sessions p99 is closer to 1.2s. With Dedicated + tuned batching and our new KV cache configuration, we've modeled meeting the 600ms p99 objective for typical request patterns. that's why we suggested reserved capacity sized to your traffic profile.

Roadmap & Feature Requests
[03:46] Jordan Lee: On product roadmap items you asked about — longer context support, advanced caching hooks, and improved observability for token-level cost breakdowns are in the roadmap Q2/Q3. Priya can give timelines.
[03:58] Priya Kapoor: Longer-context model variants scheduled in Q2 beta; advanced caching hooks (prefix pinning and manual cache invalidation) are Q3. Observability token-level breakdown is rolling to GA in May. we'll share feature flags for early access.
[04:14] Aisha Khan: Can we trial the long-context beta for 2 weeks to test edge cases with our data shape?
[04:20] Jordan Lee: Yes we can enable beta access, see action items.

Technical Deep Dive Highlights
[04:29] Priya Kapoor: Quick technical note — we ran a profiling pass on your top 10 request patterns. The biggest wins were: persistent KV cache (saves 30% tokens on repeat prompts), merging a set of small requests into micro-batches (saves 12-18% cost), and int8 quantization on the LLM for non-production workloads gave 1.6x throughput.
[04:51] Marcus Doyle: On the quantization, what are the quality tradeoffs? our QA team flagged a hallucination increase on patient-medical nuance prompts in an in-house run.
[05:00] Priya Kapoor: Good flag. For clinical decision support we recommend keeping fp16 for production; quantization is useful for dev/ingest or lower-stakes rerank/embedding pipelines. we can run a controlled eval on your prompt set to measure regressions.

Compliance & Security
[05:20] Jordan Lee: On SOC2/SAML/SSO — we have the SOC2 Type II report and SAML SSO integrations ready; documents are in the security folder. For KMS/HSM and VPC peering we have a standard playbook for Dedicated and Private customers.
[05:34] Leah Chen: We'll need an architecture review with our security team and cloud infra to validate VPC peering and EGRESS rules.
[05:41] Jordan Lee: We'll schedule that. Priya we'll include the network diagram and a checklist for their infra reviewers.

Benchmarks & Next Steps
[05:50] Priya Kapoor: We'll run a 10k token benchmark on 8xA100 Dedicated nodes with your prompt set; results will include latency distribution, token cost estimates, and a recommended capacity size.
[06:00] Jordan Lee: Action items recap at the end will capture owners and due dates.

Questions asked by Customer:
[06:09] Aisha Khan: 1) Can we get per-route cost breakdowns in the console? 2) Can you provide SLA language for Dedicated production? 3) Are there any known limitations with US healthcare datasets?
[06:19] Priya Kapoor: 1) Yes token-level and route-level breakdowns are available, GA in May. 2) We'll send the Dedicated SLA doc. 3) No special limitations, but we recommend keeping PHI in a private deployment and applying data minimization; we also have a HIPAA playbook.

Recap & Close
[06:35] Jordan Lee: Recap — we'll send updated pricing and capacity recommendation, run the benchmark, enable long-context beta access, and schedule a security architecture review. any last questions?
[06:47] Leah Chen: No, that covers it. thanks everyone.
[06:53] Aisha Khan: Thanks Jordan and Priya.
[06:56] Jordan Lee: Thanks all, talk soon.

End of transcript
